answer: Verifiers in six regions ping each ID at random times, and the round-trip latencies pin it to a rough spot on the map. IDs that land in the same spot split one reward cap, so a rack running a thousand keys earns like one agent. Each extra fake needs its own server in a distinct city, and a proxy can add delay but never remove it. Cheap cities fill first, so the fiftieth fake rents a box on some remote mesa at ten times the price. Even a whisper of shared clock jitter links hosts, and the payout tide stays flat.
